objective: Create and completely implement mermansi, a production-quality pure Rust terminal renderer library and CLI for Mermaid. Before broad implementation, create root AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, and docs/SUPPORT_MATRIX.md that enumerate all TODOs, architecture boundaries, licenses, and measurable final gates. Treat merman-core 0.8.0-alpha.3 RenderSemanticModel as the authoritative semantic inventory: Json, Mindmap, State, Sequence, Flowchart, Architecture, Class, C4, Kanban, Gantt, Pie, Packet, Timeline, Journey, Requirement, Sankey, Radar, Info, Treemap, Block, Er, QuadrantChart, XyChart, GitGraph, TreeView, Ishikawa, EventModeling, and Venn; also inventory parser aliases and transformed families including graph aliases and ZenUML. Use merman-core as the single strict parser and semantic source. Reuse merman-ascii where it satisfies the contract, and implement adapters for every remaining family without copying or rewriting the Mermaid parser and without forking Selkie. beautiful-mermaid is MIT-licensed algorithmic prior art only, never a byte oracle. Every successfully parsed built-in family must produce deterministic nonempty ASCII and Unicode output through one public source-to-text API and the mermansi CLI; no family may silently drop parsed semantic entities, relationships, labels, endpoints, markers, hierarchy, or chart values. Use terminal-native geometry where it is meaningful and an explicitly documented structured terminal representation where exact browser geometry is not meaningful; never disguise a summary as full geometric parity. Implement optional ANSI roles without affecting geometry. Build a display-column-aware bounded canvas using grapheme segmentation, Unicode width, continuation cells, merged directional strokes, atomic overwrite behavior, and deterministic routing. English, Chinese, combining-mark, and emoji labels must preserve geometry; boxes must close; relationships retain endpoints, markers, and labels; applicable TD/TB/BT/LR/RL directions, self-relations, cycles, disconnected components, nested groups, parallel and dense relations must be tested; source, row, column, cell, routing, and output allocations must be bounded and return typed errors; output must be deterministic. Pin a usable Rust toolchain because Merman requires Rust 1.95 and this host has 1.97.1 installed. Keep parser integration, semantic adapters, layout/routing, canvas, ANSI encoding, CLI, and tests in separate modules following KISS, YAGNI, DRY, and SOLID. Maintain an executable support-matrix conformance test so every current upstream semantic enum variant and supported parser family is accounted for, with at least one English and one Chinese semantic fixture per family. Implement coherent plan phases through the repository issue-loop, Review actual diffs, resolve every finding through numbered Issues, run all configured checks, and create a separate Conventional Commit for each reviewed work unit. Completion requires all TODOs done, every matrix row implemented and tested, no open Issues, a final clean Review, all verification commands passing, and every reviewed unit committed.

steps.description: Verify sanitize_label_text in src/ansi.rs is pub(crate) and handles: CSI (ESC [ ... final 0x40..=0x7e), string-control families (OSC ESC ], DCS ESC P, APC ESC _, PM ESC ^, SOS ESC X) consuming through embedded non-terminating ESC bytes and stopping only at BEL (0x07) or ST (ESC \), and all C0/DEL/C1 controls including TAB/LF/CR via ch.is_control().

Verify the Pie adapter (src/adapters/pie.rs) calls sanitize_label_text before the format! width-calculation line for every ColorMode, with an accurate comment noting it is the primary defense layer and is currently called only by the Pie adapter.
Correct any doc/comment in src/ansi.rs or src/adapters/pie.rs that inaccurately claims every adapter calls sanitize_label_text; confirm it says 'Currently called only by the Pie adapter'.

Verify integration tests in tests/semantic_integrity.rs: (a) Plain-mode output has zero ESC and zero BEL bytes, (b) visible label text survives, (c) Value-column offset is identical for sanitized vs clean labels, (d) Ansi16 and TrueColor modes assert the exact user-supplied CSI \x1b[31m and OSC \x1b]0;X are absent while renderer's own ESC count > 0 and BEL count == 0, (e) ST-terminated OSC is stripped in Plain mode.
Run cargo test --test semantic_integrity and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings after cargo clean; confirm all pass with zero warnings.

implementation.summary: Preserved durable Pie-label sanitizer (sanitize_label_text in src/ansi.rs handling CSI, OSC/DCS/APC/PM/SOS string-control families consuming through embedded non-terminating ESC to BEL/ST, and all C0/DEL/C1 controls including TAB/LF/CR via ch.is_control), Pie adapter calling it before width calculation in every ColorMode, pub(crate) visibility, accurate 'Currently called only by the Pie adapter' doc comment, Plain/Ansi16/TrueColor integration assertions (user-supplied CSI and OSC absent, renderer's own ESC allowed, BEL==0), visible-label and Value-column alignment tests. Strengthened with new unit tests for all five string-control families and embedded-ESC-in-DCS consumption, plus three new integration tests for DCS stripping in Plain/Ansi16/TrueColor modes. All 35 semantic_integrity tests pass and strict Clippy is clean after cargo clean.

summary: Active Issue 0002 is fully resolved. sanitize_label_text in src/ansi.rs (pub(crate)) handles CSI (ESC [ ... final 0x40..=0x7e), all five string-control families (OSC ESC ], DCS ESC P, APC ESC _, PM ESC ^, SOS ESC X) consuming through embedded non-terminating ESC bytes to BEL (0x07) or ST (ESC \), nFe escapes, bare ESC, and all C0/DEL/C1 controls including TAB/LF/CR via ch.is_control(). The Pie adapter calls sanitize_label_text before the format! width/layout line for every ColorMode — this is the primary defense, not a final String strip. The lib.rs strip_ansi call is a secondary Plain-mode safety net only. Visible label text (Red, AB) survives sanitization. Malicious and normal labels produce identical Value-column offsets (proven by pie_value_column_aligns_with_sanitized_and_clean_labels). Colored modes (Ansi16, TrueColor) reject the exact user-supplied CSI \x1b[31m, OSC \x1b]0;X, and DCS \x1bPpayload while retaining renderer-owned ESC roles and zero BEL. ST-terminated OSC is stripped. Canonical semantic JSON is serialized via serde_json::to_value with proper JSON string escaping — not destructively changed — because sanitize_label_text is applied only to section.label in the Pie table, not to the structured model. Strict Clippy passes with -D warnings. All 35 semantic_integrity tests pass, including the required regression test asserting zero ESC bytes in Plain output.

resolutions.description: Pie labels with raw ANSI escape sequences no longer leak through --no-color output. sanitize_label_text strips CSI, all string-control families (OSC/DCS/APC/PM/SOS) with embedded-ESC consumption and BEL/ST termination, plus all C0/DEL/C1 controls (TAB/LF/CR) before Pie width/layout calculation in every ColorMode. Regression tests verify zero ESC/BEL in Plain output, identical Value-column alignment for sanitized vs clean labels, renderer-owned roles retained in colored modes, and visible text preserved.
